newsitem.title: CANADA: No weekend flood risk seen on Manitoba's Red River.
newsitem.headline: No weekend flood risk seen on Manitoba's Red River.

text.p: There is no risk of the Red River flooding over the long Easter weekend, a Manitoba Natural Resources (MNR) official said on Wednesday.
"We'd need a few days of temperatures above this just because there's so much snow," MNR's manager of Water Planning and Development Larry Whitney said.
The temperature in Winnipeg at 1300 CST Wednesday was five degrees Celsius (41 Fahrenheit).
Floodwater levels in the Red River Valley were expected to be one to 1-1/2 feet higher than last year's flood based on normal spring weather, forecasters said.
Precipitation for the month of March has been below average in Manitoba but above average in the U.S. portion of the Red River watershed.
A rapid snow melt or heavy spring rain could see levels three to five feet higher than 1996 between the U.S. border and Winnipeg.

Last year's flood delayed spring seeding of wheat, barley, canola, flax and corn by one month, reducing the frost-free crop growing window. The Red River Valley accounts for two percent of Prairie acreage but 3.5 percent of grain output, according to the Canadian Wheat Board.

The U.S. portion of the Red River watershed saw three times the average annual snow accumulation this winter while the Canadian side saw twice the average accumulation. There is a 10 percent chance this could be the watershed's worst flood of the century, MNR said.
"The snow mitigates against the higher temperatures and it takes a while for run off to actually start under these conditions," Whitney said.
Environment Canada forecast temperatures Thursday to reach the freezing point with freezing rain or snow expected for the Red River Valley.
Significant flooding is expected in southeast Manitoba on the Brokenhead River, Whitemouth River and Whiteshell River.
Assiniboine River flooding between St. Lazare and Brandon was forecast to be similar to last year, MNR said.
Souris River flooding near the U.S. border was projected to be similar to last year.
